content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"A disciple is a committed learner-follower of Jesus who obeys his teaching, imitates his life, accepts the cost of following, and bears fruit; in mainstream usage the term is effectively coextensive with 'Christian'/every genuine believer (Acts 11:26), with narrower historical uses (the Twelve) and generic uses (adherent of any teacher) as secondary senses.","book_summary":"A disciple is one who continues under the Master until the law is sealed inwardly (Isa 8:16; Jer 31:33) and teaching bears obedient fruit; the disciple 'enters the Name' (Ex 23:21; Rev 14:1), accepts the full cost (Luke 14:26-33), and is perfected to be as his Master (Luke 6:40). The book explicitly flags the common view ('any believer, entered by faith and baptism') as the view it is departing from.","consensus_core_identification":"Disciple = any committed follower/learner of Jesus, the normative identity of every Christian believer.","book_core_identification":"Disciple = one who perseveres under the Master to completion — the law sealed within, the Name entered, the cost fully accepted, perfected into the Master's likeness — i.e., a completed/sealed follower rather than any believer.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The consensus admits all genuine believers as disciples from the point of faith onward; the book excludes believers who have not continued to completion (John 8:31 'if ye continue... then are ye my disciples indeed'), have not had the law inwardly sealed, or have not forsaken all. The Rev 14:1 citation further hints that the disciple class is identified with a sealed remnant bearing the Father's name (the 144,000), reclassifying ordinary believers-in-progress as not-yet-disciples. This is close to the two-tier/higher-commitment reading the consensus lists as a minority alternative, plus the 'elite sealed class' reading Response C lists as rare.","material_contradiction":"","rationale":"The book retains the consensus's central referent — a learner-follower of Jesus formed into the Master's likeness (Luke 6:40, John 8:31, Luke 14 are shared proof texts) — so the core category is intact, not replaced. But it materially tightens the conditions: discipleship is completed/sealed perseverance ('until His law is sealed within,' 'perfected'), and its common-view note explicitly rejects the 'any believer' scope. Extension shrinks from all believers to those who persevere to a sealed, perfected state, matching REFINED (narrowing at the boundary) rather than DIVERGENT (no replacement of the referent).","citation_support":"PARTIAL","strongest_objection":"One could argue for MATCH: every element the book emphasizes (continuing in the word, counting the cost, becoming like the teacher, law written on the heart) is drawn from the same passages the consensus itself cites as defining discipleship, so the book may just be stating the ideal of discipleship rather than restricting who counts as a disciple. Against this, the book's own common-view note frames 'any believer, entered by faith and baptism' as the merely 'commonly taught' position it is correcting, and the Ex 23:21/Rev 14:1 'enters the Name' linkage (144,000 with the Father's name) goes beyond consensus usage — indicating deliberate narrowing, not restatement. The Ex 23:21 and Rev 14:1 citations do not on their own establish that 'disciple' denotes this sealed group, which is why citation support is only partial.","confidence":"high"}
